hypothesis: A full 32-lane warp owning a 32x32 tile may improve the warp-register transpose by producing one fully coalesced 32-float store segment per instruction and avoiding multiple warps for each tile. This mapping costs five exchange stages (16 lane/register pairs per stage, 80 shuffle calls per tile) and 32 values per lane, so register pressure or shuffle cost could outweigh the mapping benefit. Grouping four independent tile-owning warps in a CTA may reduce CTA scheduling overhead without requiring shared memory or a block barrier; controller timing and build diagnostics must decide.
notes: The proposal uses one 32-lane warp per tile; each CTA has four independent warps, each assigned a different tile column. The tile-row grid is capped and the kernel strides across further tile rows, while every tile exchange remains within one warp. Unsigned shuffles and bitcasts avoid floating-point arithmetic. No build or timing output for this proposed source is available in this action, so its register count, spills, correctness, and repeated full-run n=1024 timings are unmeasured. Existing n=1024 samples were 3.3350, 3.4902, 3.4515 us for the 8x8 candidate and 3.4147, 3.3904, 3.3411 us for the 16x16 candidate; baseline samples were 17.1338, 16.7488, 16.8746 us. The provided 16x16 ordinary build output only reports an unused BLOCK_ROWS warning and contains no register or spill evidence. transformations: Replaced the active naive launch with four independent warps per CTA; each warp handles one 32x32 tile, with tile rows assigned by a capped-grid stride so positive n divisible by 32 remains covered.

Each lane loads 32 rows for its input column, then five unrolled same-warp XOR-shuffle stages exchange lane and register index bits. The exchanges use unsigned values and avoid shared memory and CTA-wide synchronization.
After the exchanges, each lane owns one original input row and stores 32 values to contiguous output columns using size_t indexing and bitcasts for exact float-bit copies.
